content.value_statement: Complex applications often strain when reads and writes share one model. This skill provides CQRS templates for commands, queries, projections, and consistency handling.
actual_capabilities: Explains CQRS components and when to use the pattern.
Provides Python templates for commands, command handlers, and a command bus.
Provides query, query handler, pagination, and read database examples.
Shows FastAPI routes that separate command and query endpoints.
Includes read model synchronization and read-your-writes consistency patterns.
limitations: Example code needs integration with real repositories, databases, and event stores.
The templates are Python-centric and use FastAPI examples.
Production concerns such as authentication, tracing, and migrations are not fully implemented.
The skill does not include executable tests or package files.

use_cases.title: Split Read And Write Models
use_cases.description: Design a service where commands change state and queries read optimized views.

use_cases.title: Plan Event-Sourced Workflows
use_cases.description: Map commands, events, projections, and checkpoints before implementing an event-driven system.

use_cases.title: Improve Reporting Performance
use_cases.description: Create denormalized read models for dashboards and customer order queries.

prompt_templates.title: Explain CQRS Fit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to explain whether CQRS fits my order management service. Include benefits, costs, and simpler alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Design Command Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design commands, command handlers, and validation rules for creating and cancelling orders.

prompt_templates.title: Build Query Side
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design query handlers, read models, pagination, and filters for customer order history.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Projection Recovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan projection synchronization, checkpointing, rebuilds, and read-your-writes consistency for an event-sourced service.

output_examples.input: Design CQRS for an order service with customer order history.
output: A command side with create, add item, and cancel operations.
A query side with order detail and customer order history views.
A projection plan that updates read models from order events.

output_examples.input: Improve stale read handling after a write command.
output: A consistency strategy that waits for an expected event version.
A timeout path that returns data with a stale data warning.
A checkpoint approach for tracking projection progress.

best_practices: Start with clear command and query boundaries before adding event sourcing.
Use denormalized read models that match real query needs.
Define acceptable consistency lag and recovery procedures early.
anti_patterns: Do not introduce CQRS for simple CRUD workflows without scaling pressure.
Do not share one schema between write models and read models.
Do not ignore projection failures, checkpoints, or rebuild requirements.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design CQRS services with commands, queries, read models, projections, and consistency handling.

faq.question: Does it require event sourcing?
faq.answer: No. It includes event-sourced patterns, but CQRS can be used without a full event store.

faq.question: Which language do the templates use?
faq.answer: The examples use Python, with FastAPI shown for HTTP endpoints.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Is the sample code production ready?
faq.answer: No. It needs real persistence, authentication, observability, tests, and deployment-specific hardening.

faq.question: When should teams avoid CQRS?
faq.answer: Avoid it when a simple CRUD model meets performance, consistency, and reporting needs.
